text: WPS9284 is the Policy Research Working Paper "Simulating the Potential Impacts of COVID-19 School Closures on Schooling and Learning Outcomes: A Set of Global Estimates" (World; document date and disclosure date 2020-06-18; document ID 32145839).

Abstract (from the record): School closures due to COVID-19 left more than a billion students out of school. The paper simulates three, five and seven months of closure with different mitigation effectiveness (optimistic, intermediate, pessimistic scenarios), using data on 157 countries. COVID-19 could cost 0.3 to 0.9 years of learning-adjusted schooling, bringing effective basic schooling down from 7.9 years to 7.0-7.6 years; close to 7 million primary and secondary students could drop out because of the income shock alone; the current cohort could lose $355, $872 or $1,408 in yearly earnings ($6,472 to $25,680 over a lifetime in present value). A five-month shutdown could generate learning losses with a present value of $10 trillion, up to 16 percent of government investment in this cohort's basic education, and the goal of halving learning poverty by 2030 could be missed without drastic remedial action.
